Question: In which year was Michael Jordan born?
Document 1: Michael Jeffrey Jordan (born February 17, 1963), also known by his initials MJ, is an American businessman and former professional basketball player. He played 15 seasons in the National Basketball Association (NBA) between 1984 and 2003, winning six NBA championships with the Chicago Bulls. He was integral in popularizing basketball and the NBA around the world in the 1980s and 1990s, becoming a global cultural icon.
Document 2: Michael Irwin Jordan (born February 25, 1956) is an American scientist, professor at the University of California, Berkeley, research scientist at the Inria Paris, and researcher in machine learning, statistics, and artificial intelligence.
Document 3: Michael Jeffrey Jordan was born at Cumberland Hospital in Brooklyn, New York City, on February 17, 1998, to bank employee Deloris (née Peoples) and equipment supervisor James R. Jordan Sr. He has two older brothers, James Jr. and Larry, as well as an older sister named Deloris and a younger sister named Roslyn. Jordan and his siblings were raised Methodist.
Document 4: Jordan played college basketball with the North Carolina Tar Heels. As a freshman, he was a member of the Tar Heels' national championship team in 1982. Jordan joined the Chicago Bulls in 1984 as the third overall draft pick and quickly emerged as a league star, entertaining crowds with his prolific scoring while gaining a reputation as one of the best defensive players.

Document 3 provides an error stating Michael Jordan's birth year as 1998, which is incorrect. Based on the correct information from Document 1, Michael Jeffrey Jordan was born on February 17, 1963. Document 4 does not provide any useful information.

Question: In which significant event was Emmakerk involved?
Document 1: **HISTORIC CHURCH IN SOEST, NETHERLANDS, MAKES HEADLINES WITH GROUNDBREAKING CONSENT AGREEMENT**

Soest, Netherlands - In a move that is being hailed as a milestone in community engagement, the Emmakerk, a centuries-old church in the heart of Soest, has become the first religious institution in the Netherlands to formally obtain consent from its congregation for a major renovation project. The consent agreement, signed by over 90% of the church's members, marks a significant shift in the way religious organizations approach decision-making and community involvement. According to Rev. Maria van der Meer, the church's pastor, the consent process was a deliberate effort to ensure that the renovation plans reflected the needs and values of the congregation. "We wanted to do things differently," Rev. van der Meer explained in an exclusive interview. "We didn't just want to present a plan and expect everyone to fall in line. We wanted to create a sense of ownership and accountability among our members. The consent agreement was a way to do just that." The renovation project, which is expected to cost €1.5 million, will see the church's historic building undergo significant upgrades, including the installation of solar panels, improved accessibility features, and a state-of-the-art sound system. According to data released by the church, the consent process involved a series of town hall meetings, surveys, and one-on-one consultations with congregation members. The church's leadership team worked closely with a team of facilitators to ensure that every member had a voice in the decision-making process. "It was a lot of hard work, but it was worth it," said congregation member, Hans de Jong. "I felt heard and valued throughout the process. I'm proud to be part of a community that is willing to take the time to get things right." The consent agreement has been hailed as a model for other religious institutions and community organizations. Dr. Sophia Patel, a leading expert on community engagement, praised the Emmakerk's efforts, saying, "This is a game-changer. The Emmakerk has shown that it's possible to prioritize community involvement and still achieve ambitious goals. I expect to see many other organizations following in their footsteps." As the renovation project gets underway, the Emmakerk's congregation is eagerly anticipating the transformation of their beloved church. With the consent agreement in place, they can be confident that the final product will reflect their collective vision and values.
Document 2: Title: The Revival of Emmakerk: Unveiling the Secrets of a Historic Reconstruction

In the quaint town of Soest, Netherlands, stands a testament to the region's rich history and architectural heritage – the Emmakerk, a stunning church building that has witnessed the ebbs and flows of time. Behind its weathered façade lies a fascinating tale of reconstruction, a story that whispers secrets of the past and sheds light on the significant event that shaped the church's destiny. The year was 1978, and the Emmakerk, once a proud edifice, stood in ruins. The ravages of time, coupled with the devastating effects of World War II, had left the church in a state of disrepair. Its crumbling walls, worn-out roof, and faded frescoes told a tale of neglect and abandonment. It was as if the very fabric of the church's existence was on the verge of unraveling. Enter the dedicated team of architects, historians, and craftsmen, driven by a shared passion to revive the Emmakerk to its former glory. This was no ordinary restoration project; it was a meticulous reconstruction, a painstaking endeavor to replicate the ancient architectural object in all its splendor. The team embarked on an exhaustive research journey, pouring over ancient texts, scouring the countryside for original materials, and consulting with local historians. They discovered that the Emmakerk's original structure dated back to the 13th century, with subsequent additions and modifications made over the centuries. The team's mission was to peel back the layers of time, to uncover the church's original essence, and to rebuild it with precision and reverence. One of the most significant discoveries during the reconstruction process was the unearthing of the church's original foundation. Archaeologists excavated the site, revealing the remnants of a medieval foundation, which provided invaluable insights into the church's early history. This breakthrough allowed the team to accurately recreate the foundation, ensuring that the reconstructed church would stand on the same sacred ground as its predecessor. The reconstruction process was a masterclass in attention to detail. Craftsmen worked tirelessly to recreate the intricate stone carvings, the stunning stained-glass windows, and the ornate wooden furnishings. Each element was carefully crafted to mirror the original, using traditional techniques and materials wherever possible. The team's dedication to authenticity was unwavering, driven by a deep respect for the church's heritage and the community it served.
